column1: # NAMED CONSTRAINT ALIASES -- the `type()`-marked definitions block.
# The algebra has no int8/uint16/port keyword and does not need one: a
# constraint is a value, so a name for one is a field, and `type()`
# keeps the definitions out of the output while they still unify.
# docs/design/AONTUCONSTRAINTS.0.md wanted sized-integer sugar built
# into the language (its "free win" once bounds exist); these rows are
# why that was declined -- the idiom is already expressible, and unlike
# a keyword it composes and is not a closed list.
# Normative: docs/reference-language.md "Named constraint aliases";
# task form in docs/how-to.md "Name a reusable constraint". Both are
# executed by ts/test/docs.test.ts, so these rows and those pages
# cannot drift apart silently.
# Every expectation was obtained by running BOTH engines and diffing
# full output, per the parity probe. Columns: name<TAB>mode<TAB>src<TAB>expect
alias-uint8-accepts
alias-uint8-rejects-above
# The refusal lands at the field that holds the value, not at the
# definition -- an agent reading `path` is sent where the fix goes.
alias-uint8-rejects-path
# LEAD WITH THE KIND. This is the trap the idiom invites and the reason
# every alias in the documentation starts with `integer`: bounds alone
# bound a NUMBER, so a float in range satisfies them. Both rows are
# correct behaviour; they are here as a pair so the difference is a
# pinned contract rather than a surprise.
alias-kind-named-rejects-float
alias-kind-omitted-admits-float
# `type` is not a reserved word -- the mark does the work, not the name.
alias-key-name-not-reserved
# Aliases are ordinary values, so they compose both ways: one defined
# in terms of another, and one met with a further constraint at the
# point of use.
alias-of-alias
alias-narrowed-at-use
# A VIOLATED COMPOSED ALIAS NAMES THE WHOLE RESIDUAL (BUGS.md 48).
# The constraint error's own hint promises that `expected` is "the
# normalised residual the value must satisfy", and these rows hold both
# engines to it. When the referent is completed by a LATER statement the
# reference resolves a pass late, so the locally-conjoined atom reaches
# the field as a PEER of an expectation -- and an expectation rebuilt
# from its original peg dropped it. The value stayed enforced, but the
# canon lost it and the refusal named only whichever atom happened to
# reject: `a:20` said `max(15)`, `a:1.5` said `integer&min(0)&max(255)`,
# neither the residual. An expectation now carries the meet as its peg.
alias-violated-names-residual
alias-violated-code
alias-violated-path
# The SAME residual whichever atom the value offends -- the kind, the
# lower bound, the alias's own ceiling, or the one added at the point of
# use. Each of these named a different value before.
alias-violated-by-kind
alias-violated-by-lower
alias-violated-by-alias-ceiling
# CANON IS WHAT THE EVALUATOR ENFORCES. This is the half that made the
# defect more than a message: the canon of the composed alias dropped
# `max(15)`, so `-c` printed -- and `aontu hash` pinned -- a document
# admitting 20, which the original rejects. The two ports also hashed it
# differently, which is a parity break at the trust layer.
alias-composed-canon
# The plain (unmarked) layering that reaches the same path, so the fix
# is pinned independently of the `type()` mark.
alias-layered-canon
alias-layered-violated
# Unlayered controls: these always agreed, and pin that the fix did not
# buy the layered answer by changing the direct one.
alias-direct-canon
alias-nested-canon
# THE TRUST-LAYER CONSEQUENCE, pinned directly. `aon1-` is what pins
# meaning; the two ports produced DIFFERENT hashes for the marked form
# and both produced a hash of the wrong document for the layered one.
# A hash row asserts the exact digest, so it fails on any canon drift
# that a canon row somehow missed.
alias-composed-hash
alias-layered-hash
